title: Security remediation: close 2 critical + 7 high findings, migrate Terraform state, narrow the CI/CD trust boundary
context: Derived from .claude/plans/build-a-remediation-plan-squishy-lightning.md (the approved remediation plan) and .claude/plans/security-review-2026-08-12.md (the source review: 2 critical, 7 high, 16 medium findings, five parallel reviewers, findings re-verified against the live Cloud Run service). Two findings are live exposure: /api/upload/complete stores a client-supplied gcsKey that the download route later signs against a bucket where the app SA holds objectAdmin, and the public /g/<slug> page serializes bcrypt token_hash values for the group and every member file into anonymous HTML while its token gate is client-side only. Two controls that look active are dead: the hourly cleanup job has never run (verified in production: scheduler reports code=5, the endpoint 307s to /login before its own OIDC check), and the login rate limiter is keyed to a URL the server-action login never requests. Every production secret sits in plaintext in local Terraform state. Owner decisions: one comprehensive branch; migrate state then rotate all secrets; upgrade both next (to 16.2.12 — the GitHub Advisory DB gives firstPatchedVersion 16.2.11 for every open advisory, so 16.3.0 is unnecessary) and next-auth (exact 5.0.0-beta.32); the pre-token group page shows the group name only. IMPORTANT: tasks 11-13 are operational. Their deliverable is config changes plus a verified runbook — no implementer executes a production mutation (no terraform apply, no init -migrate-state, no secret rotation, no branch-protection PUT, no gcloud/gh write). The owner runs those steps; each task carries a critical AC enforcing that boundary.
verification: npm run lint && npm test && npm run build

Task 12 depends on 11 (terraform module as a unit; AUTH_URL variable and image ignore_changes must land before the migration runbook's first post-migration plan) and takes .gitignore after tasks 10 and 11. 6 and 12 are fully disjoint.
Alone, depends on task 12. Rotation runbook must not exist before the backend migration, or rotated secrets land straight back into a local plaintext state file.

security_findings.description: The now-live gcs backend block names a globally-unique bucket (pubsec-fileshare-tfstate) that does not yet exist, in a public repo where the name has been visible for months. terraform init -migrate-state resolves the name against whoever owns it; a squatted, world-writable bucket would receive every production secret in plaintext. The runbook's Step 5c verification succeeds against any readable bucket and would not catch this.
security_findings.remediation: Add an ownership assertion to tfstate-migration.md between Steps 2 and 4 (gcloud storage buckets describe --format='value(project_number)' compared against the expected project) and state that a 409 from Step 2's create is a hard stop; or rename the bucket to include the project number so the name cannot have been pre-registered.

security_findings.description: The true object size from GCS metadata is never compared against MAX_FILE_SIZE — the 10 GB cap is enforced only against the request body's self-reported size, so any actor with upload permission (including a 15-minute agent key) can PUT an object of any size to the signed URL. This is the residual task 1's evaluator routed to audit triage; task 1's omission rationale was incorrect.
security_findings.remediation: After the !objectMeta guard, reject objectMeta.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE with a 400 and deleteFromGCS(gcsKey); add a test asserting an over-cap statObject result yields 400 with insertFile not called.

security_findings.description: The new anonymous credential-verification endpoint emits no log on a failed token check (only the 500 handler logs), unlike every sibling secret-verifying path added this cycle — a distributed token-guessing campaign leaves no trace; the only other control is the per-IP, per-instance in-memory limiter, which also logs nothing.
security_findings.remediation: Add a rejection log to the 401 branch mirroring the download route's format (slug and outcome server-side only; response bodies stay byte-identical to preserve the ac4 non-oracle property).

tasks.title: C1: derive the GCS object key server-side and verify the uploaded object
tasks.why: Any actor with upload permission — including a 15-minute agent key — can currently register an arbitrary object name in a bucket where the app service account holds objectAdmin, then download it with their own token; this is the single widest live exposure in the app.

acceptance_criteria.text: POST /api/upload/complete never reads gcsKey from the request body; the persisted gcs_key and filename are derived server-side from the validated sha256 plus the filename extension. A request posting gcsKey: 'secrets/prod-key.json' results in insertFile receiving gcs_key '<sha256>.<ext>'.

A shared deriveGcsKey(sha256, filename) in src/lib/upload-meta.ts is the only producer of object keys, used by both prepare and complete. The extension is path.extname lowercased and gated by /^[a-z0-9]{1,8}$/ with a 'bin' fallback, so deriveGcsKey(sha, '../../etc/passwd') contains no '/' and no '..'.

complete calls a new statObject(gcsKey) in src/lib/gcs.ts (getMetadata, null on 404, rethrow otherwise) and returns 400 when the object is absent; the persisted size comes from GCS metadata, not from the request body.
validateUploadMeta applies identical rules in prepare and complete, and the content-type pattern is end-anchored and length-capped so 'text/plain\r\nX-Injected: 1' is rejected by both.
normalizeSha256() validates and lowercases; an uppercase digest for existing content takes the collision branch instead of creating a second row and a second token.
A duplicate sha256 at complete returns 409 with a constant body, not a 500 carrying a SQLite 'UNIQUE constraint failed' message.
Both upload routes return { error: 'Internal server error', phase } and log the real message via console.error, matching the admin-route convention.

Dead code removed: computeSHA256AndStream in src/lib/sha256.ts and streamToGCS in src/lib/gcs.ts (both zero callers), plus the now-stale streamToGCS entry in the vi.mock factory at src/tests/unit/admin-route.test.ts:23.

New tests/unit/upload-meta.test.ts covers the traversal, extension and content-type cases; tests/unit/upload-route.test.ts is extended to assert a caller-supplied gcsKey is ignored, that a missing object yields 400 with insertFile not called, and that the 500 body is never err.message.

tasks.notes: Do NOT delete getGCSReadStream or renameInGCS from src/lib/gcs.ts — grep confirms scripts/migrate-to-sha256.ts:47,74,98 still consumes both. Rejected alternative: an HMAC handshake between prepare and complete. The key is a pure function of two inputs the server already validates, so an HMAC would re-transmit recomputable data, add a secret to rotate, and still could not prove the object exists. Deliberate non-goal: server-side SHA-256 verification. GCS exposes only crc32c/md5Hash, so real verification means streaming the object back through Cloud Run — the exact cost the signed-redirect design exists to avoid. Document sha256 as a client-asserted content address and leave the dedup-poisoning residual (upload/route.ts:60-68) noted rather than fixed. Do not add x-goog-content-length-range: statObject already enforces the size bound before anything is recorded, and the header would need to be added to every uploader including external agents.

tasks.title: C2b: make the group token gate server-side and stop leaking the manifest
tasks.why: An anonymous visitor to /g/<slug> currently receives the bcrypt token hashes for the group and every member file plus the full inventory, and the token form only calls setSubmitted(true) — so the listing was never actually protected.

acceptance_criteria.text: An anonymous GET of /g/<slug> returns HTML containing no '$2b$', no token_hash, no gcs_key, and no file listing. Verified by a test that inspects the returned element's props and by curl against a running instance.

Per the owner's decision the pre-token page shows the group name only — no file count, no expiry, no listing. The page fetches just the name via getGroupNameBySlug and calls notFound() for a slug that fails isValidSlug.
POST /api/groups/[slug]/access verifies the submitted token against the group's bcrypt hash server-side and returns { name, expires_at, files } as PublicGroupFile objects only on success.
An unknown slug and a wrong token produce byte-identical 401 bodies and both perform exactly one bcrypt compare, so the route is neither an existence oracle nor a timing oracle.
An expired group returns 410 only after the token verifies; member files whose own expires_at has passed are excluded from the manifest.
The group download route applies the same per-file expiry check after token verification, so a long-lived group can no longer serve an expired file.
New tests/unit/group-access-route.test.ts and tests/unit/group-page-leak.test.ts cover ac1, ac4, ac5 and assert the page passes no group data prop at all.

tasks.notes: Rejected alternative: a server action returning the manifest. tasks.title: H1: make /api/cleanup reachable and correct
tasks.why: Verified in production: the proxy 307s the Cloud Scheduler request to /login before the route's own OIDC verification runs, so the hourly cleanup has never executed and every file with an expiry is still in GCS.

acceptance_criteria.text: A request to /api/cleanup carrying an Authorization: Bearer header reaches the handler and receives the handler's 401, not a 307 redirect to /login.

src/proxy.ts exports selfAuthenticatingRoute(pathname) returning 'agent-key' for /api/upload*, 'route' for exactly /api/cleanup, and null otherwise, replacing bearerAllowedPath. /api/cleanup is NOT added to isPublicRoute — deny-by-default is preserved and an unauthenticated crawler still gets the redirect.

verifyOidcToken fails closed: it returns false when OIDC_AUDIENCE or CLEANUP_SCHEDULER_SA is unset, and requires payload.email === CLEANUP_SCHEDULER_SA. Today an unset env var silently disables the identity check.
Audience precedence becomes CLEANUP_AUDIENCE ?? AUTH_URL so the scheduler audience is pinnable independently of AUTH_URL, and the inline require('crypto') at route.ts:43 becomes a top-level import.
A GCS delete that rejects with code 404 still removes the DB row and counts toward deleted; any other error leaves the row and is counted in errors. Today a missing object is retried hourly forever.
Expired device sessions are pruned in the same handler via getExpiredDeviceSessions + deleteDeviceSession, giving that db.ts helper its first production caller.
A cleanup rate-limit category exists so unauthenticated hammering cannot drive verifyIdToken's outbound fetch to Google's certs.

New tests/unit/cleanup-route.test.ts covers: no Authorization -> 401; valid-shaped token with CLEANUP_SCHEDULER_SA unset -> 401; wrong SA email -> 401; GCS 404 -> row deleted; GCS 500 -> row survives and is counted.

tasks.title: H2/H3/H4/H5: make authorization DB-authoritative, throttle logins by transport, trust the right proxy hop, verify the OIDC claim
tasks.why: Four independent authentication defects compound each other: admin rights survive demotion and deletion for up to 30 days, password guessing is unthrottled, every rate limit is bypassable with one header, and SSO grants admin on an unverified and mis-parsed email claim.

acceptance_criteria.text: getIsAdmin() resolves permissions from the database by session.user.id rather than the JWT claim. A session whose JWT says permissions ['admin'] but whose DB row says [] returns false; a session for a deleted user returns false.

Failed-login throttling lives inside the credentials authorize path (exported as authorizeCredentials for testability), keyed on both username and client IP, so it cannot be bypassed by changing transport. Five failures for one username followed by the CORRECT password still returns null.

A verifySecret(candidate, hash | null) helper in src/lib/token.ts performs exactly one bcrypt compare against a fixed dummy hash when the record is absent, and is used for the unknown-user path, the OIDC-user-with-null-hash path, the group access route, the group download route and the single-file download route. Unknown username and wrong password both perform exactly one compare.

getClientIp is moved to src/lib/throttle.ts, exported, and reads from the right-hand end of x-forwarded-for with a TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS override defaulting to 0. Given 'x-forwarded-for: 1.2.3.4, 9.9.9.9' it returns 9.9.9.9, and rotating the leftmost entry across many calls does not reset the counter for the real IP.

resolveOidcUserPermissions requires email_verified === true and derives the domain via a helper that returns null unless there is exactly one '@' with text on both sides, accepting the hd claim as an alternative domain source. An email claim of 'victim@example.com@attacker.io' does not auto-promote, and an unverified profile never gets a session (signIn callback gate).
session.maxAge is set to 8 hours in src/auth.ts, and resolveUploadActor re-resolves permissions from the DB when a cookie session is present (agent Bearer keys, capped at 15 minutes, are unchanged).

The sliding-window limiter moves into src/lib/throttle.ts and src/proxy.ts re-exports isRateLimited and getRateLimitCategory, so the existing tests/unit/proxy.test.ts imports from @/proxy keep working. getRateLimitCategory gains an optional method parameter and returns 'login' for POST /login.

New tests/unit/admin-auth.test.ts, throttle.test.ts and login-throttle.test.ts cover ac1-ac4; tests/unit/oidc.test.ts is extended for ac5 including the assertion that upsertOidcUser is not called with ['upload','admin'] for the double-@ email.
